description:
Parse the 231 code_aster/Behaviours/*.py declarations into a generated Rust
registry: enum variants, num_lc, state-variable names and counts, supported
modelisations and deformations, integration algorithm. No physics yet.

Also in P0, and now ENLARGED by the maintainer's 2026-08-04 finite-strain
decision:

- Pin the Voigt convention with a round-trip test between code_aster's
  sqrt(2)-scaled shear ordering and the SymmTensor OFFBEAT inherits from
  outram-foam-basic-lib. A mismatch here silently corrupts every shear term in
  every law downstream, and announces itself in no test that was not written to
  catch it.
- Carry a FINITE-STRAIN kinematic layer: deformation gradient, logarithmic
  (Hencky) strain, and the GDEF_LOG pre/post-processing code_aster wraps its
  small-strain laws in. This was originally deferred; the maintainer decided on
  2026-08-04 to design for finite strain from the start, because retrofitting it
  after the laws are written is a rewrite rather than a patch.
- Make the kinematics boundary with OFFBEAT explicit. OFFBEAT's MechanicsSolver
  is small-strain; these laws will not be. That difference must be visible in
  the API rather than implied.

Acceptance: the registry compiles, round-trips every catalogue entry, NORTON
dispatches end-to-end to a stub, the tensor round-trip test passes for a general
(non-symmetric-shear) stress state, and the Hencky strain reduces to the
small-strain tensor in the infinitesimal limit.
title: code_aster P0: catalogue ingestion, registry generation, Voigt + finite-strain kinematics

description:
Found while building the kovan-tui Ingest tab (interactive PDF import with a metadata review step), 2026-08-05.

Three gaps in kovan-literature's public API that kovan-tui had to work around:

1. NO PUBLIC IDENTIFIER DERIVATION (the important one). make_slug/make_id are private in crates/kovan-literature/src/metadata.rs and run exactly once inside extract_metadata. After a human corrects a wrong year/author, there is no way to ask the library to re-derive slug and id, so kovan-tui MIRRORS both functions in crates/kovan-tui/src/tui/ingest/metadata.rs (kept byte-for-byte compatible, pinned by a test reproducing the library's own doe2021test case). Real duplication that will drift. Proposed fix: pub fn derive_identifiers(doc: &mut KovanDocument) (or slug_for/id_for free functions) so both the TUI and any future corrector call the same code.

2. NO PROGRESS REPORTING. extract_metadata / pdf_to_markdown are all-or-nothing blocking calls with no callback and no page counter, so a UI can only show elapsed time (kovan-tui runs it on a worker thread and shows elapsed + a spinner, deliberately never a fabricated percentage). A per-page callback or an iterator over pages would let a real progress indicator exist honestly.

3. NO PER-FIELD PROVENANCE / CONFIDENCE. extract_metadata knows which source each field came from (Info dictionary, eScholarship cover page, text fallback) but discards it, so a reviewer cannot see which fields are guesses. Exposing e.g. title_source/year_source would make review screens sharper — arguably what a documented best-effort extractor owes its reviewer.

Motivating real case: importing the 1977 Argonne report ANL-7416 Supplement 2 yields title correct, year 2004 (the scanner's digitisation date), empty authors (real corporate author: Argonne Code Center), slug 2004anl7416. Correcting it in the TUI must produce argonnecodecenter1977anl7416 — which today needs the mirrored algorithm.

Context: crates/kovan-tui/DECISIONS.md, section 'Ingestion pass' (2026-08-05).
title: kovan-literature: expose public identifier derivation + extraction progress/provenance hooks

description:
Maintainer wants the boiling detail in the steam-generator widgets done carefully -- bubbles are the thing that gives away a boiling surface, and getting them wrong makes an otherwise good drawing read as decoration.

CURRENT STATE (b42df8f, crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/steam_generator.rs):
  - Horizontal U-tube (VVER): bubbles rise off the tube bundle.
  - Vertical U-tube (PWR): entrained droplets drawn in the steam space above the water level.
  - Helical coil: once-through, no level and no bubbles -- correct, leave alone.

Both are deterministic scatters seeded from a hash, which must stay true (the widget is rebuilt every repaint; a real RNG makes them shimmer).

WHAT 'FUSSY' SHOULD MEAN -- candidate list, to be refined by the maintainer:
  - Bubbles should NUCLEATE AT THE HEATED SURFACE, i.e. originate on the tubes, not appear uniformly in the water volume.
  - Bubble size should GROW as they rise -- coalescence plus falling static head. A uniform bubble size is the tell.
  - Void fraction should INCREASE UP THE BUNDLE in a recirculating SG, so the population should be denser and larger near the top of the heated length.
  - Density should scale with DUTY, so the bubble field responds to the power/temperature sliders rather than being static decoration.
  - Nothing below the level should be a droplet and nothing above it a bubble -- the two populations must not cross the free surface.
  - Rise should be plausible: roughly vertical, slight wobble, faster for larger bubbles.

NOT YET SPECIFIED: the maintainer has not said which of these bothers them most. Ask before doing all of it -- some are cheap and some (a real void profile) are not.

CONSTRAINT: this is offline demonstration ARTWORK, not a two-phase model. outram-foam-multiphase has real void/CHF/wall-boiling closures but they are not wired to anything and must not be dragged in for a drawing. Keep it a display heuristic and keep saying so in the docs.
title: Steam generator widgets: bubble generation needs to be physically fussy

description:
crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/solid_database/ contains fecral.rs and generic_heating_element.rs, but SolidMaterial (mod.rs:58) has no Fecral and no GenericHeatingElement variant. Those property modules are therefore unreachable through the enum -- dead code that a reader will mistake for available materials.

Fix: either add the enum variants and wire the match arms, or delete the modules.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.
title: tuas: fecral.rs and generic_heating_element.rs unreachable — no SolidMaterial variant

description: New workspace crate: reusable visualization framework depending on tampines, nee_soon (reactor-vessel/instrumentation), chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator. Provides visual process objects (Pipe, Pump, Valve, HeatExchanger, SteamGenerator, Turbine, Condenser, CoolingTower, ReactorVessel, Instrumentation) whose rendering derives directly from physics state (cell count -> displayed cells, temperature -> cell color, mass flow -> tracer direction, residence time -> tracer travel time). Philosophy: avoid separating physics and rendering unnecessarily -- components bundle physics state + visual representation + animation logic together. Approved plan: outram-park-dt-plan.md (workspace root), Part 3. Unlike tampines, GUI deps (egui/eframe/egui_plot/egui_extras) are real dependencies here, not dev-only -- this crate makes no Android-portability claim (presentation-layer only).
title: outram-park-digital-twin-engine — reusable visualization framework + reactor simulators

description:
Maintainer: defer until later. Steam-generator bubble work (the 'ngeow' bead) is higher priority and should be done first -- both would share the same deterministic-scatter machinery, so doing SG first makes this cheaper.

IDEA: draw cavitation in the pump widgets (crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/pump.rs).

Cavitation is LOCALISED AND DIAGNOSTIC, not diffuse -- which is what makes it worth drawing. Vapour forms where local static pressure falls below saturation: the SUCTION SIDE OF THE BLADE LEADING EDGES NEAR THE IMPELLER EYE, where velocity is highest and pressure lowest. It should appear as a cloud hugging the leading edges, growing along the blade as NPSH margin falls, and collapsing further out where pressure recovers -- that collapse is what erodes impellers.

Drawn well it reads instantly as 'this pump is in trouble', which is the kind of thing an operator-facing twin should show.

INPUT NEEDED: one scalar -- available NPSH against required, or simply a margin fraction in [0,1].

CONSTRAINT: offline demonstration artwork, not a two-phase model. Same rule as the SG bubbles -- put the bubbles where the physics puts them, but keep it a display heuristic and say so.

Applies to PumpKind::Centrifugal and VerticalCannedRotor. The axial propeller cavitates differently (tip vortex) and is lower value.
title: Pump widgets: cavitation bubbles at the impeller eye (DEFERRED)
